title: Things to Do in Ooty: Toy Train, Tea Gardens, Lakes & Nilgiri Views
seoTitle: Things to Do in Ooty: Toy Train, Tea & Views | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Ooty: the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, the Botanical Garden and Rose Garden, Ooty Lake, Doddabetta Peak, a tea factory visit, Pykara falls and lake, Avalanche Lake, Toda villages, Coonoor and Kotagiri, Mudumalai safaris and homemade chocolate.
dek: The Queen of the Nilgiris, a Raj-era hill station at over 2,200 metres, reached by a rack railway and surrounded by tea estates, eucalyptus and shola grasslands.
searchIntent: Families and couples planning two or three days in Ooty and the Nilgiris, often with Coonoor and Mudumalai.

hero.caption: Nilgiri Mountain Railway

intro: Ooty (Udhagamandalam), at about 2,240 metres in the Nilgiri hills, was developed from the 1820s by John Sullivan, the Collector of Coimbatore, and became the summer headquarters of the Madras Presidency. It is home to the Toda, Badaga and other Nilgiri communities, and is surrounded by tea estates, eucalyptus and the remains of shola grasslands.

The things to do in Ooty include the UNESCO-listed Nilgiri Mountain Railway, the Botanical Garden and Rose Garden, boating on Ooty Lake, Doddabetta Peak, tea factories, lakes and waterfalls, and trips to quieter Coonoor and Kotagiri and the wildlife of Mudumalai.
Two to three days is ideal. March to June is peak season; October to December and early spring are clearer and quieter. Weekends and May are very crowded.

See the view from Doddabetta Peak
Visit a tea factory and museum
Go on a safari in Mudumalai

items.name: Ride the Nilgiri Mountain Railway
body: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway, part of the UNESCO-listed Mountain Railways of India, climbs from Mettupalayam to Ooty via Coonoor, using a rack-and-pinion system on the steepest section. The full journey takes about five hours uphill through tunnels, forests and tea estates. Seats sell out quickly; book early. A shorter ride between Coonoor and Ooty is also possible.

facts.Time needed: About 5 hours for the full ride

items.name: Walk through the Botanical Garden
body: The Government Botanical Garden, laid out in 1848, has terraced lawns, a fossilised tree trunk, rare plants and a glasshouse. The annual flower show in May draws huge crowds.

facts.Best time: Morning; May for the flower show

items.name: See the Rose Garden
body: The Government Rose Garden, on terraces on Elk Hill, has thousands of rose varieties and is at its best from about April to June.

items.name: Go boating on Ooty Lake

image.alt: Ooty Lake with boats and hills
image.caption: Ooty Lake

body: Ooty Lake, created by John Sullivan in 1824, has rowing, pedal and motor boats, a small train for children and pony rides along the shore.

items.name: See St Stephen's Church and Stone House
body: St Stephen's Church, built in 1829, is one of the oldest churches in the Nilgiris, with timber said to have come from Tipu Sultan's palace. Stone House, Sullivan's residence and the first bungalow in Ooty, is nearby.

items.name: See the view from Doddabetta
body: Doddabetta, at about 2,637 metres, is the highest peak in the Nilgiris. A road leads almost to the top, where a telescope house looks out over the hills. Mornings are clearest.

items.name: Visit a tea factory
body: Tea factories and museums near Doddabetta and in Coonoor show how Nilgiri tea is processed, with tastings and shops. Homemade chocolate, eucalyptus oil and Ooty varkey biscuits are other local buys.

items.name: See Pykara falls and lake
body: Pykara, about 20 km away, has a waterfall that flows in steps over rocks and a lake with boating, surrounded by grassland and pine. Shooting spots and the pine forest are on the way.

items.name: Visit Avalanche Lake
body: Avalanche Lake, about 28 km away in shola forest and grassland, is visited through a forest department eco-tourism jeep ride with limited numbers. It is one of the most beautiful and least crowded spots around Ooty.

items.name: Visit a Toda settlement
body: The Toda, a pastoral community of the Nilgiris, live in settlements called munds, with distinctive barrel-shaped huts. The Tribal Research Centre Museum near Ooty explains Nilgiri communities; visits to munds should be respectful and guided.

items.name: Explore Coonoor
body: Coonoor, about 20 km away and quieter than Ooty, has Sim's Park, a botanical garden with rare plants, and viewpoints such as Dolphin's Nose and Lamb's Rock over deep valleys and tea estates. The fruit show is held in May.

items.name: Visit Kotagiri
body: Kotagiri, the oldest hill station in the Nilgiris, has quiet tea estates, Catherine Falls and the Kodanad viewpoint over the plains and Moyar valley.

items.name: Go on a safari in Mudumalai
body: Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, about 35 km down steep hairpin bends, has jeep and bus safaris for elephants, gaur, deer and occasionally tigers and leopards. The Theppakadu elephant camp is nearby.

items.name: See the Pine Forest and Shooting Spot
body: The pine forest on the Ooty–Thalakunda road has tall trees on a slope running down to a lake, and nearby 9th Mile (Shooting Spot) is a grassy hilltop where many films have been shot.

items.name: Visit Emerald Lake
body: Emerald Lake, in the Silent Valley area, is a quieter reservoir surrounded by tea gardens, good for a picnic and sunrise.

items.name: See the Needle Rock viewpoint
body: Needle Rock viewpoint at Gudalur, on the road to Mudumalai, gives a wide view over the forests and the Mudumalai plains.

items.name: See the Deer Park and Thread Garden
body: The Deer Park beside Ooty Lake and the Thread Garden, with flowers handmade entirely from thread, are easy stops for families.

items.name: Catch the summer festival
body: In May, the Nilgiris hold a series of shows: the flower show at the Botanical Garden, the rose show, the fruit show at Sim's Park in Coonoor and the vegetable show in Kotagiri. Book stays early.

items.name: Summer (March to June)
body: Peak season, when the plains are hot and Ooty is pleasantly cool. Gardens are in full bloom and the May shows draw large crowds.

items.name: Monsoon (July to September)
body: Heavy rain, mist and green hills. The toy train can be disrupted by landslides, but hotels are quieter and cheaper.

items.name: Winter (October to February)
body: Clear skies and cold nights, with frost in December and January. A lovely time for views and walks.

byTraveller.text: The toy train, Botanical Garden, Ooty Lake boating and Doddabetta.
Stay in Coonoor or a quiet estate, see Avalanche Lake and Pykara, and enjoy the tea gardens.
Avalanche Lake, Mudumalai safaris and walks in Kotagiri.
Ride the full Nilgiri Mountain Railway from Mettupalayam, then take the Coonoor–Ooty section again in the other direction on another day.

oneDay: Start at Doddabetta for the morning view and visit a tea factory on the way down. Walk through the Botanical Garden and Rose Garden, go boating on Ooty Lake in the afternoon and end with a stroll through the market for chocolate and tea.
tips: Coimbatore airport is about three hours away; Mettupalayam is the railhead for the toy train.
Book the toy train well ahead, especially in summer.
Carry warm clothes; nights are cold year-round and frosty in December and January.
Weekend traffic in town can be heavy; walk where possible.
Traffic on the Mettupalayam and Gudalur ghat roads is heavy on weekends; start early.
Buy chocolate, tea and eucalyptus oil from established shops rather than roadside stalls.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Ooty?
faqs.a: Ride the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, visit the Botanical Garden and Rose Garden, boat on Ooty Lake, see Doddabetta, visit a tea factory, see Pykara and Avalanche Lake, and explore Coonoor, Kotagiri and Mudumalai.

faqs.q: How long is the Ooty toy train ride?
faqs.a: About five hours from Mettupalayam to Ooty uphill. Shorter sections, such as Coonoor to Ooty, are also possible.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Ooty?
What is the best time to visit Ooty?
faqs.a: March to June for pleasant weather, and October to December for clear skies and fewer crowds.

faqs.q: Is Ooty good for a family trip?
faqs.a: Yes. The toy train, lake boating, gardens, Doddabetta and nearby wildlife make Ooty one of South India's classic family holidays.
Coonoor is smaller, quieter and greener, with tea estates and viewpoints such as Dolphin's Nose. Ooty has more attractions and activities. Many visitors stay in one and visit the other on a day trip.
